text:
infra-bot: Pager triggered: spike in regional fallback churn across us-east <-> us-west <-> eu. Rate of fallback events up 12x over baseline. Symptoms: 5xx errors for a subset of requests, token latency higher, and increased retry traffic. Graph: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/1976543210 :rotating_light:

alex (on-call): acknowledged. paging rotation: @maria and @ben are on-call for this shift, paging both. joining bridge in 2.

maria (eng-sre): I'm on it. quick hypothesis: health-check hysteresis too aggressive (stable_count=1) + aggressive fallback policy order is flipping between regions when transient packet loss hits control plane. can we set fallback.enabled=false globally while we triage? that will stop the route churn.

inc-bot: Runbook: http://runbooks/redwood/region-fallback. Steps: 1) mute alerts 2) disable fallback policy 3) pin critical tenants if needed 4) increase health_check.stable_count 5) gather pcap/logs.

ben (eng-runtime): agree with disabling fallback. also we should pin the model variant for top-10 customers to avoid model-variant fallback during region moves. command to pin: `rvctl models pin --tenant <tenant-id> --model redwood-xxl-v1`

alex (on-call): executing mitigation now:
```
# disable automatic region fallback globally
rvctl routing update --policy fallback --set enabled=false --scope global
# response
{"status":"ok","policy":"fallback","enabled":false}
```

maria (eng-sre): thanks. running quick health probes against nodes implicated: `curl -sS http://node-us-east-1/health | jq .`

maria (eng-sre): sample failing lines from node logs: 
```
2026-03-15T13:09:12Z node-us-east-1 healthcheck timeout=2000ms attempts=1 -> marking UNHEALTHY
2026-03-15T13:09:12Z node-us-east-1 fallback-trigger route=us-west reason=healthcheck:timeout
2026-03-15T13:09:13Z node-us-west-3 healthcheck ok attempts=1 -> marking HEALTHY
2026-03-15T13:09:14Z node-us-east-1 healthcheck ok attempts=1 -> marking HEALTHY
2026-03-15T13:09:14Z routing engine: apply fallback to us-east
```

maria (eng-sre): you can see stable_count=1 is the problem: a single probe causes unhealthy->healthy transitions and the routing policy immediately flips. patch suggestion: set `health_check.stable_count=3` and `interval=5s` to require three consecutive failures before marking unhealthy.

ben (eng-runtime): posting current routing config for visibility: 
```
routing:
  fallback:
    enabled: true
    order: [us-east, us-west, eu]
    health_check:
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 2s
      stable_count: 1
```

alex (on-call): created bridge: https://meet.redwood/incident/1976543210 - folks join if you're doing live changes. muted noisy alerts in grafana for this alert.

sarah (product): any customer impact numbers? which tenants saw errors? we need to notify support and assigned CSMs if >3 customers affected.

maria (eng-sre): quick query: `SELECT tenant, count(*) FROM request_logs WHERE status>=500 AND ts > now()-15m GROUP BY tenant ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 20;` returns three customer IDs with elevated 500s: tenant-231, tenant-88, tenant-412. I recommend pinning those three while we stabilize.

ben (eng-runtime): pin commands executed for tenant-231 and tenant-88; tenant-412 is on a rolling upgrade, coordinating with infra to avoid interference.

maria (eng-sre): applying config change to increase stable_count and keep fallback disabled until we confirm:
```
rvctl routing update --policy fallback --set health_check.stable_count=3 --set health_check.interval=5s --scope global
# response
{"status":"ok","policy":"fallback","health_check":{"stable_count":3,"interval":"5s"}}
```

alex (on-call): re-run health probes and watch routing decisions.

maria (eng-sre): after change and 2 minutes observation: fallback churn rate down from 12x to ~1.1x. 5xx error rate for affected tenants dropped by 85%. graphs attached to bridge.

ben (eng-runtime): re-enable fallback with conservative settings? I'd prefer to keep globally disabled until next maintenance window, and instead rely on manual failovers. Recommend change: `enabled=true` but add `cooldown_seconds=30` and `stable_count=3`. That will reduce flip-flopping.

alex (on-call): notes: re-enable? hold — product asked for customer notifications first. i'll coordinate with support.

sarah (product): please draft customer note to CSMs: short summary + mitigation + ETA for final fix. i'll send once we have final config.

maria (eng-sre): creating ticket INC-1976543210 in PagerDuty -> assigned to eng-sre. Postmortem owners: @maria, @ben.

inc-bot: Incident severity set to SEV2 (widespread retries + customer impact). On-call handover in 1h to ops-evening rotation.

alex (on-call): handoff: @jordan (ops-evening) is paged to take over at 15:30 UTC. leaving bridge open. summary: root cause likely mis-configured health-check hysteresis causing rapid unhealthy/healthy flips triggered by transient packet loss between regions -> routing policy flips -> fallback churn -> increased retries and 5xxs. mitigations applied: global fallback disabled, stable_count increased to 3, critical tenants pinned. next step: plan for config validation gate to prevent stable_count < 2 in prod and add circuit-breaker to routing service.

maria (eng-sre): follow-ups: 1) postmortem 48h 2) deploy config validation in CI 3) add synthetic probes from multiple regions and alert when healthcheck flip rate > 5/min.

ben (eng-runtime): logging improvement: tag routing-change events with `change_id` and emit diff for easier correlation.

alex (on-call): closing active pager now; monitoring for 30m. if we see relapse, re-open. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

maria (eng-sre): assigning doc and runbook updates to sprint. will include snippet of commands used and timeline.

sarah (product): thanks team. I'll prepare customer copy for support and sync with CSMs.

inc-bot: Incident updated: status=stabilized, severity=SEV2 -> monitoring.

ben (eng-runtime): leaving final note: recommend adding an automated test that runs `routing policy` through randomized packet loss scenarios at deploy-time; low effort, high value.
